discovery.note: Looks at every pump.fun / PumpSwap buy of 0.5+ SOL: did other wallets pile in within ~3 s, and could a fast copier have sold higher 4-6 s later. A candidate needs 6+ such buys, a wave after half or more, and a typical move of +3% or better. Read-only. Prices include the traders' fees, so moves are slightly pessimistic. A candidate is a lead to test, not proof.

history.note: Looks back 14 days at each listed wallet's first buys of a token and reads what traded in the minute after. Move = from the price paid one or two blocks behind the wallet to the price about 10 s later, before our own fees; "won" = better than +3%. Good = not a bot, 30+ buys, and passing (half or more won, average above +3%) on BOTH the older and the newer half of its buys. History is not a live fill: a lead to test, not proof.

slow.note: Paper and read-only. CANDIDATES: the listed wallets, the busiest pump.fun buyers, and (day holders) wallets that bought 0.2+ SOL of coins that keep trading for days (3+ days old, no stables or staked SOL: on 12 of Jupiter's lists, or verified with $50000+ traded in a day; and coins our wallets traded on 3+ days), sampled at 0.25 / 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 13 days back, 3 pages each. A full first page inside 3 h = bot; 10+ trips in its newest 200 transactions with a median hold under 10 min = fast (flipper); neither is read further. A wallet read in full that neither passes nor is near (10+ trips, median hold 30+ min, ahead) keeps its numbers but not its swaps and is read again every 14 days; passing and near ones daily. SCREEN: each candidate's own SOL swaps over the last 30 days as round trips (first buy until 90% sold). Passes = not a bot, 20+ trips, first sell a median 30+ min after its first buy, realised SOL positive in BOTH halves of the period, 40%+ won, no single trade half or more of the profit. Realised SOL is before network fees. LATE: for its newest 30 trips, a copier entering 30 s / 5 min after its first buy and selling 30 s after its first sale, priced from other people's trades, 1% cost taken off: an estimate. smallStartPct = trips whose first buy was under half the wallet's usual. PAPER: followed wallets copied live with 0.25 SOL at Jupiter quotes, 5 s / 30 s / 5 min / 30 min after we see the buy, sold 5 / 30 s after its first sale (or at 72 h). Leads to test, not proof.

links.note: For each seed wallet (public fomo traders): MONEY = plain transfers of SOL, dollars or coins with another wallet, also one step further; TIMING = wallets that started holding the same coin in the half hour before the seed bought it, on 3+ coins. Each such wallet is then read itself: shared = coins both bought, before = it bought first (beforeWithin1h: within the hour before), soldInto = it sold within half an hour after the seed's buy, overlapPct = share of its own coins that the seed also bought. "likely" = a money link AND first on 3+ shared coins (twice as often as second). A money link = 2+ plain transfers, or one of $10000+ or 50+ SOL. Evidence, not proof of ownership. Looks back up to 30 days: daysRead says how far the read naming the wallet and the read of its dollar accounts each got, daysCovered is the shorter of the two, buysFromDaysAgo is how old its newest and oldest buy in the read are. transactionsRead = [naming the wallet, touching its dollar accounts, a short stretch of all its token accounts]; a coin received for nothing is not a money link. Wallets shown as short tags.

replay.note: REPLAY of the seeds' own past buys, from each coin's record: an estimate, not a result. A copy enters at the middle price the coin traded at in the 3 blocks after the seed's buy (the seed's own price when nobody traded there) and is sold at the price of the last trade at or before each hold. 2.8000000000000003% is taken off for buying and selling (what the real test's 0.05 SOL copies lose in and out). Likely KINDER than reality: our own order moves nothing here, and when a crowd follows a real copy pays more than the middle price (the real test paid a median 2.5% over the wallet, far more in a crowd). hardEntry = the same copies bought at the highest price of those blocks. Not in it: a sale that fails, a coin that cannot be sold. target10 = sold at the first hold up 10%, else at 60 s. checked = buys looked at, buys = those that could be priced, noRecordAfter = the coin's record held nothing after the buy. A return is capped at +1000%.

exitStudy.note: Paper, fastest copy only, after costs. Checks are at fixed times, so a spike between two checks is missed. The 3 to 10 minute checks exist only for buys seen since 11 Nov 2026 18:00 KST. `target10` = sell at the first check up 10%, else at 60 s.

byWave.group: strong first wave (15+ follower transactions in ~4 s)

byStart.group: up strongly at 5 s (10% or more)

sizeStudy.note: Paper. The fastest copy priced at 0.05, 0.25, 1, 3 SOL at the same moment and sold 10, 30, 60 s later, with network fees of 0.0001 SOL per in-and-out (what the real test pays; the other paper rules assume 0.002). A stake with no quote is left out of its row, so a big stake's row can miss the thinnest pools.

lateStudy.note: Paper. Only buys priced at every entry time (0, 1 s after we know), so the rows compare like with like. 0 s is the instant quote: no order gets it, a real one lands about 1 s later. Each entry is sold as soon as it is up 10% after costs, else 60 s after its own purchase (holdOnly = no target, just the 60 s). priceVsFastestPct = how much more (+) or less (-) that entry paid than the instant quote (median). risingPct = share of buys where it paid more.

walk.note: Paper. Only buys known since 2026-11-11T16:15:00.000Z (after the pace rule was written), 0.25 SOL each, bought the moment we know, sold at +10% or after 30 s (t30) and 60 s (t60). t60sl10 / t60sl15 / t60sl20 = the 60 s rule, sold sooner at the first check (2, 5, 10, 20, 30 s) where the copy is 10% / 15% / 20% down (the real test looks every 0.75 s, so it stops sooner and more often than this). late1... = the same rules bought 1 s after we know, nearer to where the real test's buy lands (its gap is still the one of the moment we know). calm = the trader had bought fewer than 3 times in the 3 hours before; gap = how far our price already was above the wallet's.

hours.note: Paper, every stored buy. By the hour of the day in KST (3 hour blocks): the copy sold at +10% or 60 s, bought the moment we know (t60), bought 1 s later (late1t60, about where the real test lands) and that with a 15% stop. days = on how many different days the block has buys: one day is not a pattern.

repeats.note: Paper, every stored buy. first = no other listed wallet bought the coin in the 30 min before; second = one other did; third or later = two or more did. Same three ways of buying as in hours.

secondWave.note: Paper, every stored buy whose window was checked to the end. Buy the coin entrySec after a listed wallet bought it, if no other listed wallet bought it in between (at the sale price of that moment plus the coin's own in-and-out cost, fees included; a model, not a quoted buy). Sell 2 s after the next listed buy of the coin (withNextAt5: 5 s after), or endSec after the first buy if none comes. buyers = how many listed wallets had bought the coin in the 30 min up to that buy. firstHalfAvgPct / secondHalfAvgPct = the average of the earlier and of the later half of the copies: a pattern should show in both. nextPct = how often the next buyer came in time. waitSecMedian = from our buy to it.

buySize.note: Paper, every scored buy, split by the size of the wallet's buy: against its usual buy (the median of its 5+ earlier buys, no hindsight) and in SOL. Holdings are not recorded, so "share of the wallet" cannot be read. Buys under 0.1 SOL were never recorded. late1 = bought 1 s after we knew (where the real test landed), +10% or 60 s; late1x30 = 1 s late, sold at 30 s; instant = the moment we knew (faster than real), +10% or 60 s. Real = the real test's sent copies matched to their buy; "won" = came back with more SOL.

sameBlock.note: What if we had landed right behind the wallet: entry at the price the first followers really paid in its block or the next (where none, the wallet's price +2%), same exits. An estimate, kept apart from the real rules.

traders.note: A trader's record = every first buy of that wallet we saw, copied on paper the moment we knew and sold at +10% or 30 s. From 4 copies on: good = made money on average and half or more won; bad = lost on average and fewer than half won; mixed = between. Few copies make a noisy verdict: the rules copy-d0-trader-* judge each buy only on the copies before it.
